wtb.name: Thierry Henry
award: PFA Players' Player of the Year
wtb.blurb: Arsenal's all-time record goalscorer and the focal point of the Invincibles side that went unbeaten through the 2003–04 Premier League season.

wtb.name: Gheorghe Hagi
award: UEFA Jubilee Golden Player of Romania
wtb.blurb: Nicknamed 'the Maradona of the Carpathians', he is widely considered Romania's greatest player and lifted the UEFA Cup with Galatasaray in 2000.

wtb.name: Zinedine Zidane
wtb.blurb: Scored twice in the 1998 World Cup final and hit one of the great Champions League final goals, a left-foot volley for Real Madrid in 2002.

wtb.name: Jay-Jay Okocha
award: Africa Cup of Nations Best Player
wtb.blurb: Famed for outrageous dribbling, the Bolton and PSG playmaker inspired the terrace chant 'so good they named him twice'.

wtb.name: David Beckham
award: BBC Sports Personality of the Year
wtb.blurb: Won league titles in England, Spain, the United States and France, in a career that also included loan spells at Preston and AC Milan.

wtb.name: Roger Milla
wtb.blurb: At 38, his corner-flag celebrations made him the story of Italia 90, as Cameroon became the first African nation to reach a World Cup quarter-final.

wtb.name: Hristo Stoichkov
wtb.blurb: A key part of Johan Cruyff's Barcelona 'Dream Team' and the only Bulgarian to win the Ballon d'Or.

wtb.name: Georgi Kinkladze
award: Manchester City Player of the Year
wtb.blurb: A mesmerising dribbler who lit up Maine Road in the mid-90s. City fans still rank him among the most gifted players in the club's history.

wtb.name: Ronaldinho
wtb.blurb: Won the Ballon d'Or in 2005 and is remembered as one of the most joyful, skilful players of his generation.

wtb.name: Careca
wtb.blurb: Joined Napoli in 1987 to partner Diego Maradona, scoring in the 1989 UEFA Cup final and helping win the 1990 Serie A title.

wtb.name: Allan Simonsen
wtb.blurb: The only Dane to win the Ballon d'Or. He later surprised everyone by leaving Barcelona for Charlton Athletic in the old Second Division.

wtb.name: Diego Maradona
wtb.blurb: Captained Argentina to the 1986 World Cup, scoring both the 'Hand of God' and the 'Goal of the Century' against England in the same match.

wtb.name: Enzo Scifo
wtb.blurb: Dubbed 'the little Pelé' as a teenager, he played at four World Cups for Belgium across a 14-year international career.

wtb.name: David Ginola
award: PFA Players' Player of the Year
wtb.blurb: Swept both the PFA and FWA player of the year awards in 1999, the season he helped Tottenham win the League Cup.

mix.name: Wayne Rooney
mix.blurb: Manchester United's record goalscorer, and England's too until Harry Kane passed him in 2023.
hints: Born in Croxteth, Liverpool.
Aged 16, he scored a late winner for Everton that ended Arsenal's 30-match unbeaten run.

mix.name: Luka Modric
mix.blurb: Won the 2018 Ballon d'Or after leading Croatia to the World Cup final.
hints: Born near Zadar, Croatia. His family became refugees during the war.
Had early loan spells at Zrinjski Mostar and Inter Zaprešić.

mix.name: Lionel Messi
mix.blurb: Eight Ballon d'Ors, and a World Cup winner with Argentina in 2022.
hints: Born in Rosario, Argentina.
Joined Barcelona's La Masia academy at 13, with the club paying for his growth hormone treatment.

mix.name: Didier Drogba
mix.blurb: Scored the late equaliser and the winning penalty as Chelsea won the 2012 Champions League final.
hints: Born in Abidjan, Ivory Coast, and moved to France aged five to live with his footballer uncle.
Signed his first professional contract at Le Mans.

mix.name: Erling Haaland
mix.blurb: Set the Premier League record of 36 goals in a season in his first campaign with Manchester City.
hints: Born in Leeds while his father played for Leeds United.
Scored nine goals in one match for Norway at the 2019 Under-20 World Cup.

mix.name: Paolo Maldini
mix.blurb: Spent all 25 seasons of his career at AC Milan and won five European Cups.
hints: Born in Milan, the son of former AC Milan captain Cesare Maldini.
Made his Serie A debut aged 16.

mix.name: Mohamed Salah
mix.blurb: Liverpool's Egyptian King and a two-time African Footballer of the Year.
hints: Born in the village of Nagrig, Egypt.
Started his senior career at El Mokawloon (Arab Contractors) in Cairo.

mix.name: Andres Iniesta
mix.blurb: Scored the extra-time winner for Spain in the 2010 World Cup final.
hints: Born in the small village of Fuentealbilla, Spain.
Joined Barcelona's La Masia academy aged 12.

mix.name: Gareth Bale
mix.blurb: Wales's record goalscorer, with an overhead kick in the 2018 Champions League final.
hints: Born in Cardiff, Wales.
Came through Southampton's academy at the same time as Theo Walcott.

mix.name: Thomas Muller
mix.blurb: A 2014 World Cup winner and Bayern Munich's record appearance maker.
hints: Born in Weilheim, Bavaria.
Spent his whole European career at Bayern Munich before joining Vancouver Whitecaps in 2025.

mix.name: Steven Gerrard
mix.blurb: Captained Liverpool's comeback from 3–0 down to win the 2005 Champions League final in Istanbul.
hints: Born in Whiston, Merseyside.
Joined Liverpool's academy at nine years old.

mix.name: Eden Hazard
mix.blurb: PFA Players' Player of the Year in 2015, and a two-time Premier League winner with Chelsea.
hints: Born in La Louvière, Belgium.
Played for Royal Stade Brainois as a boy before joining Lille.

mix.name: Kylian Mbappe
mix.blurb: A World Cup winner at 19, and scorer of a hat-trick in the 2022 final.
hints: Grew up in Bondy, a suburb of Paris.
Made his Ligue 1 debut for Monaco aged 16.

mix.name: Cristiano Ronaldo
mix.blurb: Five Ballon d'Ors, and the all-time top scorer in men's international football.
hints: Born in Funchal, on the Portuguese island of Madeira.
Played for Madeira clubs Andorinha and Nacional as a boy before Sporting CP.
